subject: DI04005021

body.en:
Definition / principle

Molecular diffusion is relative molecular transport caused by random thermal motion and a composition driving force. Eddy diffusion is additional transport by turbulent fluid parcels.

Detailed theory and conditions

Molecular diffusion occurs in gases and liquids even without visible mixing. In laminar flow it acts across streamlines; laminar bulk flow itself is not eddy diffusion. Turbulent eddies transport packets of fluid, but molecular diffusion finally mixes at small scales. Molecular diffusivity is a mixture property at stated temperature, pressure and composition; eddy diffusivity is an effective flow-dependent parameter and can vary with position, direction and mixing intensity. They are not interchangeable constants.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Random thermal motion તથા composition driving force થી molecular relative transport એટલે molecular diffusion. Turbulent fluid parcels થી વધારાનો transport એટલે eddy diffusion.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Visible mixing વગર પણ gases/liquids માં molecular diffusion થાય છે. Laminar flow માં streamlines વચ્ચે તે કાર્ય કરે છે; laminar bulk flow પોતે eddy diffusion નથી. Turbulent eddies fluid packets ખસેડે છે અને નાના scale પર અંતિમ mixing molecular diffusion થી થાય છે. Molecular diffusivity stated temperature, pressure તથા composition પર mixture property છે. Eddy diffusivity flow, position, direction તથા mixing intensity મુજબ બદલાતું effective parameter છે; બંને interchangeable constants નથી.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Molar rate is amount transferred per time. Molar flux is amount crossing unit area per time. Diffusivity relates diffusive flux to the composition gradient in a specified reference frame.

Detailed theory and conditions

Use total stationary-coordinate flux N for material balances and molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J in Fick’s law. The negative sign means diffusion down the composition gradient, not that every reported flux is negative. The gradient is a spatial derivative, not a concentration difference without division by distance. Diffusivity has dimensions area per time; gas values are usually much larger than liquid values. For constant total molar concentration c, Fick’s law may also use the concentration derivative. If c varies, the mole-fraction form must not be casually replaced by the concentration form.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Molar rate એટલે time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles; Molar flux એટલે unit area તથા time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles. Specified reference frame માં composition gradient સાથે diffusive flux જોડતો coefficient diffusivity છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Material balance માટે stationary-coordinate total flux N અને Fick’s law માટે molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J લો. Negative sign composition gradient ની વિરુદ્ધ transport દર્શાવે છે; દરેક numerical flux negative નથી. Gradient spatial derivative છે; distance વગરનો concentration difference નથી. Diffusivity નું dimension area per time છે અને gas values સામાન્ય રીતે liquid કરતાં ઘણી મોટી છે. Total molar concentration c constant હોય ત્યારે concentration derivative વાપરી શકાય; c બદલાય ત્યારે mole-fraction form ને સીધું concentration form ન બનાવો.

h.en: Effect of temperature,pressure and composition on diffusivity
h.gu: Diffusivity પર Temperature,Pressure તથા Composition ની અસર

body.en:
Definition / principle

Diffusivity is a transport coefficient whose numerical value requires a specified mixture, phase and thermodynamic state.

Detailed theory and conditions

For dilute gases at modest pressure, increasing temperature increases molecular motion and generally increases diffusivity; at fixed temperature increasing pressure usually decreases gas diffusivity approximately inversely. Gas correlations and their exponent are model-dependent, not a universal exact power law. Liquid diffusivity generally rises with temperature as viscosity decreases; its ordinary-pressure dependence is weaker than that of gases. Composition can change viscosity, interactions and mutual diffusivity, especially in concentrated liquids. A single average D in an integrated equation is an approximation if D varies strongly over the composition range.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Diffusivity transport coefficient છે; તેની value માટે mixture, phase તથા thermodynamic state જણાવવા પડે છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Modest pressure ના dilute gases માં temperature વધતાં diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Fixed temperature પર pressure વધતાં gas diffusivity આશરે inverse રીતે ઘટે છે. Exact exponent correlation-dependent છે; universal power law નથી. Temperature વધતાં viscosity ઘટે તેથી liquid diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Ordinary pressure ની liquid પર અસર gas કરતાં ઓછી છે. Composition થી viscosity, interactions તથા mutual diffusivity બદલાય છે, ખાસ કરીને concentrated liquids માં. Range દરમિયાન D ઘણું બદલાય તો એક average D વડે integration approximation છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

Binary mixture; the same local state and molar-mean reference frame. Use mutual diffusivities, not unrelated self-diffusion coefficients. c is total molar concentration and y is mole fraction.

  1. Binary composition constraint.

  2. Diffusive fluxes sum to zero in this frame.

  3. Apply Fick’s law to both species.

  4. Substitute the binary gradient relation.

  5. For a nonzero composition gradient, the mutual coefficients are equal. The zero-gradient case cannot determine a numerical D.

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

One-dimensional transport along z; vA, vB are species molar velocities and v* is molar-mean velocity. Fickian binary diffusion is assumed. D and c need be constant only for subsequent simple integration.

  1. Define total species fluxes and molar-mean velocity.

  2. Separate relative motion from bulk motion.

  3. Insert the mole-fraction form of Fick’s law.

  4. For a steady, nonreacting constant-area layer, the species flux is constant.

  5. A mixture at molar rest has NT=0. A stagnant component means NB=0 instead; bulk Stefan flow may then exist. Laminar flow can still have nonzero bulk velocity.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: define v* and J → rearrange → substitute Fick’s law → specify which flux constraint applies. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady, one-dimensional binary ideal gas; no reaction; constant T, P, ideal-gas concentration c, D and area; layer thickness L=z2−z1; NB=0. yA1>yA2 gives positive flux toward2. R must match the molar units used.

  1. Insert NB=0 into the general equation.

  2. Separate and integrate across the layer.

  3. Evaluate limits.

  4. Use pA=PyA and ideal-gas concentration.

  5. Define the logarithmic mean of the B partial pressures; use its continuous equal-endpoint limit if necessary.

  6. Equivalent form; the factor P/pBM accounts for Stefan flow.

Symbols, model and assumptions

Same steady ideal-gas, constant T, P, D and area assumptions; NA=−NB, so molar bulk flux is zero. This is not the same condition as stagnant B.

  1. Impose equal and opposite species fluxes.

body.en:
Objective and official scope

Determine the relevant diffusivity using the institution-approved gas–liquid apparatus. The common Stefan evaporation method below determines vapor A in carrier gas B above a liquid, not dissolved-gas diffusivity inside the liquid.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved diffusion cell, bath, temperature/pressure measurement, level microscope, timer and validated liquid density/vapor-pressure data. Use the actual apparatus manual if it employs a different method.

Principle and assumptions

For a quasi-steady gas film with NB=0, interface saturation and a controlled upper boundary, level retreat gives a z²-versus-time slope.ρL is liquid density, MA is kg per mole, all gas units are consistent.

Procedure and record

Under supervision establish a constant bath state, measure total pressure and reference level, then record elapsed time and diffusion length without inventing readings. Fit z² versus time and use the boundary vapor fractions appropriate to the actual rig. Report the measured room temperature rather than assuming25°C.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Only approved volatile liquids and rated apparatus; ventilation, no ignition source, and no improvised heating or gas pressurization. Check leaks, bath stability, boundary control and whether the quasi-steady model applies.

Blank observation sheet—record actual readings only

body.en:
Objective and official scope

Determine the relevant diffusivity using the institution-approved gas–liquid apparatus. The common Stefan evaporation method below determines vapor A in carrier gas B above a liquid, not dissolved-gas diffusivity inside the liquid.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved diffusion cell, bath, temperature/pressure measurement, level microscope, timer and validated liquid density/vapor-pressure data. Use the actual apparatus manual if it employs a different method.

Principle and assumptions

For a quasi-steady gas film with NB=0, interface saturation and a controlled upper boundary, level retreat gives a z²-versus-time slope.ρL is liquid density, MA is kg per mole, all gas units are consistent.

Procedure and record

Under supervision establish a constant bath state, measure total pressure and reference level, then record elapsed time and diffusion length without inventing readings. Fit z² versus time and use the boundary vapor fractions appropriate to the actual rig. Repeat at several approved stable temperatures, using temperature-specific density and vapor-pressure data. Compare D versus T, not raw evaporation rates alone.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Only approved volatile liquids and rated apparatus; ventilation, no ignition source, and no improvised heating or gas pressurization. Check leaks, bath stability, boundary control and whether the quasi-steady model applies.

Objective and official scope

Determine liquid-phase mutual diffusivity using the approved cell/method. A calibrated diaphragm-cell method is described as one suitable format, not as a prescribed GTU apparatus.

Apparatus and preparation

Two well-mixed liquid compartments, validated diaphragm-cell constant, temperature control, timer and calibrated composition assay such as conductivity for an approved dilute electrolyte.

Principle and assumptions

A concentration difference decays approximately exponentially under a constant-D calibrated-cell model. Kcell includes geometry/porosity corrections and has units m⁻²; it is not an unverified pore-size guess.

Procedure and record

Prepare approved initial concentrations, fill without bubbles and maintain prescribed mixing without driving bulk leakage through the diaphragm. Record concentration in both compartments versus time using the validated calibration. Correct for sample withdrawal or replacement. Report actual room temperature and fit log concentration difference against time.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Follow the cell-specific procedure; some rigs require another relation. Stirrer heat, temperature-sensitive conductivity, unmixed boundary layers and leakage bias D. No fabricated cell constant or measurements.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Molecular and eddy diffusion.
q.gu: Molecular તથા Eddy Diffusion ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Molecular diffusion is relative molecular transport caused by random thermal motion and a composition driving force. Eddy diffusion is additional transport by turbulent fluid parcels. Molecular diffusion occurs in gases and liquids even without visible mixing. In laminar flow it acts across streamlines; laminar bulk flow itself is not eddy diffusion. Turbulent eddies transport packets of fluid, but molecular diffusion finally mixes at small scales. Molecular diffusivity is a mixture property at stated temperature, pressure and composition; eddy diffusivity is an effective flow-dependent parameter and can vary with position, direction and mixing intensity. They are not interchangeable constants.
a.gu: Random thermal motion તથા composition driving force થી molecular relative transport એટલે molecular diffusion. Turbulent fluid parcels થી વધારાનો transport એટલે eddy diffusion. Visible mixing વગર પણ gases/liquids માં molecular diffusion થાય છે. Laminar flow માં streamlines વચ્ચે તે કાર્ય કરે છે; laminar bulk flow પોતે eddy diffusion નથી. Turbulent eddies fluid packets ખસેડે છે અને નાના scale પર અંતિમ mixing molecular diffusion થી થાય છે. Molecular diffusivity stated temperature, pressure તથા composition પર mixture property છે. Eddy diffusivity flow, position, direction તથા mixing intensity મુજબ બદલાતું effective parameter છે; બંને interchangeable constants નથી.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Rate,molar flux,diffusivity and Fick’s law.
q.gu: Rate,Molar Flux,Diffusivity તથા Fick’s Law ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Molar rate is amount transferred per time. Molar flux is amount crossing unit area per time. Diffusivity relates diffusive flux to the composition gradient in a specified reference frame. Use total stationary-coordinate flux N for material balances and molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J in Fick’s law. The negative sign means diffusion down the composition gradient, not that every reported flux is negative. The gradient is a spatial derivative, not a concentration difference without division by distance. Diffusivity has dimensions area per time; gas values are usually much larger than liquid values. For constant total molar concentration c, Fick’s law may also use the concentration derivative. If c varies, the mole-fraction form must not be casually replaced by the concentration form.
a.gu: Molar rate એટલે time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles; Molar flux એટલે unit area તથા time દીઠ transfer થયેલા moles. Specified reference frame માં composition gradient સાથે diffusive flux જોડતો coefficient diffusivity છે. Material balance માટે stationary-coordinate total flux N અને Fick’s law માટે molar-mean-relative diffusive flux J લો. Negative sign composition gradient ની વિરુદ્ધ transport દર્શાવે છે; દરેક numerical flux negative નથી. Gradient spatial derivative છે; distance વગરનો concentration difference નથી. Diffusivity નું dimension area per time છે અને gas values સામાન્ય રીતે liquid કરતાં ઘણી મોટી છે. Total molar concentration c constant હોય ત્યારે concentration derivative વાપરી શકાય; c બદલાય ત્યારે mole-fraction form ને સીધું concentration form ન બનાવો.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Effect of temperature,pressure and composition on diffusivity.
q.gu: Diffusivity પર Temperature,Pressure તથા Composition ની અસર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Diffusivity is a transport coefficient whose numerical value requires a specified mixture, phase and thermodynamic state. For dilute gases at modest pressure, increasing temperature increases molecular motion and generally increases diffusivity; at fixed temperature increasing pressure usually decreases gas diffusivity approximately inversely. Gas correlations and their exponent are model-dependent, not a universal exact power law. Liquid diffusivity generally rises with temperature as viscosity decreases; its ordinary-pressure dependence is weaker than that of gases. Composition can change viscosity, interactions and mutual diffusivity, especially in concentrated liquids. A single average D in an integrated equation is an approximation if D varies strongly over the composition range.
a.gu: Diffusivity transport coefficient છે; તેની value માટે mixture, phase તથા thermodynamic state જણાવવા પડે છે. Modest pressure ના dilute gases માં temperature વધતાં diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Fixed temperature પર pressure વધતાં gas diffusivity આશરે inverse રીતે ઘટે છે. Exact exponent correlation-dependent છે; universal power law નથી. Temperature વધતાં viscosity ઘટે તેથી liquid diffusivity સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Ordinary pressure ની liquid પર અસર gas કરતાં ઓછી છે. Composition થી viscosity, interactions તથા mutual diffusivity બદલાય છે, ખાસ કરીને concentrated liquids માં. Range દરમિયાન D ઘણું બદલાય તો એક average D વડે integration approximation છે.
